claims.text: A machine-learning model can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model would be trained on high-entropy-alloy data containing known thermal-conductivity properties.
The approach is intended to apply at operating temperatures from 300 K to 1000 K.
High-entropy-alloy composition and microstructure contain patterns related to thermal conductivity that a machine-learning model can identify.
Learning relationships among composition, microstructure, and thermal conductivity enables accurate thermal-conductivity prediction.
The machine-learning model will predict thermal conductivity to within ±10%.
Current predictions of thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys have an accuracy of only ±20–30%.
The model is applicable only to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and microstructures are similar to those represented in its training data.
Prediction accuracy may be limited by the quality and size of the training dataset.
Prediction accuracy may be limited by the complexity of the relationships among composition, microstructure, and thermal conductivity.
The hypothesis is falsified if fewer than 80% of test-set predictions are within ±10% of measured thermal-conductivity values.
